safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold notes possible urticaria/hives; generated assessment only states suspected anaphylaxis and does not mention urticaria.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to document urticaria as part of the clinical picture reduces completeness of the assessment and may affect diagnostic clarity (isolated urticaria vs evolving anaphylaxis), but the encounter still appropriately escalated care for respiratory symptoms. The likely impact is primarily on documentation quality rather than immediate management.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated states denial of lip swelling, but transcript is ambiguous (patient does not clearly deny swelling after being asked) and gold does not contain this denial.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting a denial of lip swelling when the history is ambiguous can falsely downplay a key sign of allergic reaction/anaphylaxis and could lead downstream clinicians to underestimate severity or delay time-critical treatments (e.g., epinephrine, airway vigilance). While the patient was still advised to call an ambulance, inaccurate documentation of a red-flag symptom carries meaningful risk.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Same issue as hpi-005: denial of lip swelling is not clearly supported in transcript and absent from gold.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Repeating an unsupported denial of lip swelling in ROS further reinforces an inaccurate record about a potentially life-threatening allergic reaction sign, increasing the chance of under-triage or less aggressive monitoring/treatment if relied upon. This is clinically relevant because mucosal swelling is a key anaphylaxis feature and its absence/presence materially affects risk assessment.
